::: {.project-facts}
**My role:** classification models (KNN and decision tree)<br>
**Team:** 4 members<br>
**Data:** 2,534 Zurich listings from Inside Airbnb<br>
**Tools:** [Python]{.tag} [scikit-learn]{.tag} [pandas]{.tag} [Jupyter]{.tag}
:::

## The problem

Can listing data predict things guests care about? We asked two questions:
does a listing offer a dedicated workspace, and how quickly does the host
respond to messages?

## What I did

**k-nearest neighbors (workspace or not).** Used 10 numeric predictors and a
stratified 70/30 split, scaled the features on the training data only to avoid
leakage, and tested odd values of k from 1 to 51 with 10-fold cross-validation.
The best was k = 5.

**Decision tree (host response time, four classes).** Used 16 predictors and
tuned cost-complexity pruning with 10-fold cross-validation, which produced a
tree 7 levels deep with 19 leaves.

## Results

| Model | Test accuracy | Naive baseline | Lift |
|---|---|---|---|
| KNN, dedicated workspace | 60.8% | 58.7% | +2.1 points |
| Decision tree, response time | 73.9% | 61.9% | +12.0 points |

The tree clearly beat its baseline, with host behavior variables driving most
of its splits. The KNN model only edged past its baseline, which is a finding
in itself: listing numbers say little about which amenities a place offers.

## What I learned

Always report the baseline. A model with 60% accuracy sounds fine until you see
that guessing the most common answer gets you 59%. Comparing against a naive
benchmark keeps the results honest.
